Nita's activation also needs an instant or sorcery in an opponent's graveyard, and the loop has none. Nothing is generated to restart the cycle.
citation: Bladewing's Thrall: "When a Dragon enters, you may return this card from your graveyard to the battlefield."

reason: Slasher returns tapped with two stun counters. If you sacrifice it to Altar again, it had counters on it, so the "if it had no counters on it" condition fails and it stays in the graveyard. Stun counters only come off through untap steps, so you can't repeat the sacrifice. It works once and then ends.
citation: Unstoppable Slasher: "When this creature dies, if it had no counters on it, return it..."; 701.21a (sacrifice moves it to the graveyard)

reason: Sacrificing Bronzehide Lion to Black Carriage makes it die, and it returns as an Aura enchantment. It is no longer a creature, so it can't be sacrificed to Carriage a second time. Each cycle needs a new creature to sacrifice, so the loop can't repeat indefinitely.
citation: 701.21a: a player can sacrifice only a permanent they control. Black Carriage's cost requires sacrificing a creature, and the returned Lion is an Aura with "loses all other abilities."

cards: Tergrid, God of Fright // Tergrid's Lantern
reason: The cards don't form a loop. Tergrid only triggers when an opponent chooses to sacrifice or discard, and Ob Nixilis's +1 lets them lose life instead. Setzer's coin flips are random. Casualty only works when Ob Nixilis is cast from a zone where it can be cast, and nothing here returns it to hand or recasts it. No step feeds back into an earlier one, so nothing repeats.
citation: Tergrid: "Whenever an opponent sacrifices a nontoken permanent or discards a permanent card"; casualty is an additional cost paid only as you cast the spell.

reason: Reckless Lackey is sacrificed as a cost and nothing returns it, so the loop can't repeat. It also loses mana. The Treasure it makes gives 2 mana with Kinnan (1 from the Treasure, 1 from Kinnan's trigger), but the next activation costs {2}{R}, which is 3 mana. Kinnan's other ability costs {5}{G}{U} and only looks at the top five cards, so it can't get Lackey back reliably.
citation: 701.21a – Sacrifice moves the permanent from the battlefield to its owner's graveyard; the Lackey is not returned.

reason: Emerge needs a Lashweed Lurker in hand or another castable zone, and the sacrificed creature isn't that card. Soul Collector only returns a creature to the battlefield, never to hand. Soul Collector also needs a fresh source of combat damage on the creature each turn, and nothing here provides one. So the loop can't repeat.
citation: 702.119a: "You may cast this spell by paying [cost] and sacrificing a creature rather than paying its mana cost"

reason: The loop isn't sustainable. Each pass sacrifices Apothecary (MV 2) to return itself, and that needs 2 energy. Nightmare then goes back to hand and has to be recast for 2 mana, which gives 3 energy. The Apothecary trigger gives you only one Treasure, which is 1 mana. So each pass costs a net 1 mana, and the loop runs out of mana. The opponent's Treasure doesn't help, because the poison trigger only fires if the opponent chooses to sacrifice it. Nightmare is also sorcery-speed only.

Illicit Masquerade only puts impostor counters on creatures when it enters. A creature returned by its trigger comes back as a new object with no impostor counter. Sacrificing it to Phyrexian Altar therefore doesn't trigger Masquerade, and the chain stops. Each creature that had a counter gives one trigger at most, so the loop is finite.
citation: Illicit Masquerade: "When this enchantment enters, put an impostor counter on each creature you control."

reason: Giant Caterpillar's ability sacrifices it as a cost. The Butterfly token it creates at the next end step is a 1/1 Insect token, not a Giant Caterpillar. Nothing here returns the Caterpillar, so the ability can be activated only once. Keeper of Progenitus gives extra mana when you tap a Forest, but that mana doesn't make the Caterpillar come back, so the loop can't repeat.
citation: 701.21a: "To sacrifice a permanent, its controller moves it from the battlefield directly to its owner's graveyard."

reason: Ruin Ghost can only exile and return a land you control, so it can't blink Charming Scoundrel and re-trigger its enter ability. Nothing untaps Ruin Ghost or Parcelbeast, and nothing returns mana to pay for the activations. Parcelbeast only draws or puts out the top card of the library. The cards don't form a repeatable loop.
citation: Ruin Ghost: "Exile target land you control, then return it to the battlefield under your control."
